title: Variable Group scope
description: Which Variable Groups this automation manages, which keys they are allowed to contain, and which keys must never exist in a given environment. Values are not declared here: they arrive from the CSV, and secret values never arrive at all - they are resolved from the environment variable of the same name.

applications.description: Application keys in scope. A group whose name does not match the pattern for one of these is not touched, and is not reported as drift either: it belongs to somebody else.

groupNamePattern.description: Name derived from the application and the environment. Derivation with no per-environment override is what keeps a pipeline's reference and the group's actual name from drifting apart.

declaredKeys.description: The complete key set of a managed group. A key that is not declared here is preserved if it already exists - the automation never deletes - but it is reported, because an undeclared key in a Variable Group is a configuration nobody reviewed.

name.description: Variable name. Also the name of the environment variable a secret is resolved from.

isSecret.description: A secret key is created at the sentinel and then completed by the platform owner in the portal. This automation never writes a secret value, because it could not verify what it would be replacing.

forbiddenKeysByEnvironment.description: Keys that must NOT exist in a given environment. This is not cosmetic. A pipeline agent exposes every variable of every linked Variable Group as a process environment variable, so a stray key can switch on behaviour without any YAML mentioning it and without appearing in any pipeline diff. Declaring the prohibition per environment makes the absence auditable.

manualExclusions.description: Group names deliberately left out of scope, each with the reason. An exclusion with no reason becomes folklore.
